title: Feature Engineering
subtitle: Creating and selecting features that improve model performance

content.text: Feature engineering is transforming raw data into informative inputs (features) that help the model learn.

content.code:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder

# Create a new feature
df["price_per_sqft"] = df["price"] / df["sqft"]

# Bin a continuous variable
df["age_group"] = pd.cut(df["age"], bins=[0,18,35,60,100], labels=["child","young","adult","senior"])

# One-hot encode a categorical column
enc = OneHotEncoder(sparse_output=False)
city_encoded = enc.fit_transform(df[["city"]])

# Log-transform a skewed feature
import numpy as np
df["log_income"] = np.log1p(df["income"])

content.text: Domain knowledge beats fancy algorithms. A well-engineered feature often improves accuracy more than switching models.

questions.question: What does one-hot encoding do?
options: Converts each category value into a binary column
questions.explanation: One-hot encoding creates a binary column for each category, so models can use categorical variables.

faq.a: Including a feature that directly encodes the target label (e.g., using tomorrow's price to predict today's). It makes the model look accurate but it won't generalise.
